en: The Question on the Accomplishment of a Single Purpose by Various Dharmas
"Venerable Nāgasena, these various phenomena, being distinct, accomplish a single purpose?
"Yes, Great King, these various phenomena, being distinct, accomplish a single purpose; they destroy the defilements."
“Venerable sir, how is it that these things, though diverse, accomplish a single purpose and destroy the defilements?
“Great king, it is just as an army, though consisting of diverse elements—elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry—accomplishes a single purpose and conquers the enemy host in battle.”
“In the same way, Great King, these various states, though distinct, accomplish a single purpose: they destroy the defilements.
This is the sixteenth dilemma: the accomplishment of a single function by various states.
In this chapter there are sixteen questions.
